title: Deuteronomy Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 27.

questions.question: Who commanded the people to keep all the commandments in Deuteronomy 27?
options: Moses with the elders of Israel
Aaron alone
Joshua
The Levites only
questions.correctAnswer: Moses with the elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:1 states that Moses with the elders of Israel commanded the people to keep all the commandments.

questions.question: What were the Israelites commanded to set up when they passed over the Jordan into the land God gave them?
options: Great stones plastered with plaster
An altar of gold
A large wooden cross
A tent for worship
questions.correctAnswer: Great stones plastered with plaster
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:2 commands them to set up great stones and plaster them with plaster upon crossing the Jordan.

questions.question: What should be written upon the stones set up after crossing the Jordan?
options: All the words of this law
The names of the elders
Songs of praise
The history of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: All the words of this law
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:3 instructs writing all the words of the law on the stones.

questions.question: On which mountain were the stones to be set up and plastered after crossing the Jordan?
options: Mount Ebal
Mount Gerizim
Mount Sinai
Mount Nebo
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Ebal
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:4 specifies the stones should be set up on Mount Ebal.

questions.question: What type of altar were the Israelites commanded to build on Mount Ebal?
options: An altar of stones without iron tools
A golden altar
An altar made of wood
An altar of silver
questions.correctAnswer: An altar of stones without iron tools
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:5 states the altar must be of stones and no iron tool shall be lifted upon them.

questions.question: What kind of stones were to be used to build the altar of the LORD?
options: Whole stones
Broken stones
Chiseled stones
Polished stones
questions.correctAnswer: Whole stones
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:6 commands building the altar of whole stones.

questions.question: What offerings were to be made on the altar built on Mount Ebal?
options: Burnt offerings
Grain offerings
Drink offerings
Sin offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:6 mentions offering burnt offerings on the altar to the LORD.

questions.question: What were the people instructed to do after offering peace offerings on the altar?
options: Eat there and rejoice before the LORD
Fast for three days
Sing songs of lament
Build a shelter
questions.correctAnswer: Eat there and rejoice before the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:7 instructs the people to eat and rejoice before the LORD after offering peace offerings.

questions.question: How were the words of the law to be written upon the stones?
options: Very plainly
In secret
In a foreign language
With invisible ink
questions.correctAnswer: Very plainly
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:8 states the words of the law should be written very plainly on the stones.

questions.question: Who spoke to all Israel saying, 'Take heed, and hearken, O Israel; this day thou art become the people of the LORD thy God'?
options: Moses and the priests the Levites
Joshua alone
The elders only
The tribe of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and the priests the Levites
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:9 records Moses and the priests the Levites speaking these words to Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites were instructed to plaster the stones with plaster after setting them up.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:2 and 27:4 both command to plaster the stones after setting them up.

questions.question: True or False: Iron tools were allowed to be used in building the altar on Mount Ebal.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:5 clearly states no iron tool shall be lifted upon the stones of the altar.

questions.question: True or False: The altar was to be constructed of broken stones according to Deuteronomy 27.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:6 commands the altar to be built of whole stones, not broken stones.

questions.question: True or False: The people were to rejoice before the LORD after offering peace offerings on the altar.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:7 instructs the people to eat and rejoice before the LORD after peace offerings.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 27, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Keep all the commandments commanded this day
Write all the words of the law on stones
Build an altar of stones on Mount Ebal
Offer peace offerings and rejoice
questions.correctAnswer: Keep all the commandments commanded this day
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:1 is the first instruction given, commanding the people to keep all commandments this day, before other instructions.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 27:10, what is Israel commanded to do upon becoming the people of the LORD?
options: Obey the voice of the LORD and do His commandments and statutes
Offer sacrifices on Mount Ebal
Write the law on stones
Stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people
questions.correctAnswer: Obey the voice of the LORD and do His commandments and statutes
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:10 explicitly commands Israel to obey the voice of the LORD and do His commandments and statutes, emphasizing obedience as the proper response after becoming God's people (Deuteronomy 27:9-10).

questions.question: Which tribes were instructed to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people?
options: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, Benjamin
Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, Naphtali
Judah, Reuben, Benjamin, Gad, Dan, Levi
Issachar, Asher, Simeon, Naphtali, Joseph, Reuben
questions.correctAnswer: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, Benjamin
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:12 states that these six tribes—Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin—were to stand upon Mount Gerizim to bless the people, distinguishing them from those who were to stand on Mount Ebal.

questions.question: What was the role of the Levites according to Deuteronomy 27:14?
options: To speak aloud the curses to all the men of Israel
To build the altar on Mount Ebal
To write the law on stones
To lead the tribes on Mount Gerizim
questions.correctAnswer: To speak aloud the curses to all the men of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:14 charges the Levites to loudly proclaim the curses to all Israel, serving as the public voice of the covenant's warnings (verses 14-26).

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 27:15-26, what is the intended spiritual effect when the Levites pronounce curses and the people respond 'Amen'?
options: To publicly affirm obedience to God's law and recognize consequences of disobedience
To curse their enemies and neighboring nations
To establish political alliances among tribes
To initiate a new sacrificial system
questions.correctAnswer: To publicly affirm obedience to God's law and recognize consequences of disobedience
questions.explanation: The curses pronounced by the Levites, with the people's 'Amen' response, serve to solemnly affirm the covenant's demands and the serious consequences for violating God's law (verses 15-26). This public affirmation reinforces obedience (Deuteronomy 27:10-14).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a curse in Deuteronomy 27:15-18?
options: A man who makes any graven or molten image
A man who removes his neighbor's landmark
A man who steals from the temple treasury
A man who makes the blind to wander out of the way
questions.correctAnswer: A man who steals from the temple treasury
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:15-18 lists various sins that bring curses, including making idols, removing landmarks, and misleading the blind. Stealing from the temple treasury is not mentioned in this passage.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 27:16 warn against, and what is the implied biblical virtue taught here?
options: Setting light by (despising) one's father or mother; teaching respect and honor for parents
Stealing from neighbors; teaching honesty
Neglecting the poor; teaching generosity
Idolatry; teaching faithfulness to God
questions.correctAnswer: Setting light by (despising) one's father or mother; teaching respect and honor for parents
questions.explanation: Verse 16 curses anyone who despises their parents, emphasizing the biblical virtue of honoring one's father and mother as foundational to obedience and community integrity (see also Exodus 20:12).

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 27:17 relate to the practical Christian virtue of integrity?
options: It curses those who remove their neighbor's landmark, teaching respect for others' property and honesty
It commands building altars on Mount Ebal to show faith
It encourages generosity to strangers and widows
It requires writing the law on stones to remember obedience
questions.correctAnswer: It curses those who remove their neighbor's landmark, teaching respect for others' property and honesty
questions.explanation: Removing a neighbor's landmark was a form of theft or dishonesty. The curse in verse 17 shows the importance of integrity and respecting others' rights, which are key Christian virtues.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 27:18, what is condemned, and how does this teach us about responsibility toward the vulnerable?
options: Causing the blind to wander out of the way; teaches care and guidance for those who are vulnerable
Stealing from widows; teaches generosity
Making idols; teaches faithfulness to God
Dishonoring parents; teaches respect
questions.correctAnswer: Causing the blind to wander out of the way; teaches care and guidance for those who are vulnerable
questions.explanation: Verse 18 curses those who mislead the blind, symbolizing the responsibility to protect and guide vulnerable individuals, highlighting the virtue of compassion and justice.

questions.question: What is the significance of the division of tribes between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal in Deuteronomy 27:12-13?
options: Different tribes were assigned to pronounce blessings and curses as a public covenant renewal
Some tribes were to receive land, others were not
Certain tribes were designated as priests and others as warriors
Tribes were separated based on their size and strength
questions.correctAnswer: Different tribes were assigned to pronounce blessings and curses as a public covenant renewal
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 assign six tribes to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless and six on Mount Ebal to curse, symbolizing the covenant renewal process that publicly affirms obedience and warns against disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 27:26 states that anyone who does not confirm all the words of the law to do them is cursed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:26 clearly pronounces a curse on anyone who does not confirm and do all the words of the law, highlighting the importance of full obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 27:15, it is acceptable to make a graven image if it is put in a secret place.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:15 curses anyone who makes a graven or molten image, even if it is placed in a secret place, indicating that idolatry is abominable regardless of concealment.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 27:19 teach about justice through its curse?
options: It curses those who pervert the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow, teaching impartiality and fairness
It commands sacrifices to atone for sins
It states that only priests can judge legal matters
It blesses those who give generously to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: It curses those who pervert the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow, teaching impartiality and fairness
questions.explanation: Verse 19 condemns corrupt judgment against vulnerable groups, emphasizing the biblical virtue of justice and fairness toward all, including outsiders and the defenseless.

questions.question: How does the instruction in Deuteronomy 27:11-14 show the communal responsibility of Israel in upholding God's law?
options: By assigning tribes to publicly pronounce blessings and curses and having Levites declare the covenant, it involves all Israel in covenant renewal
By requiring each family to build their own altar
By commanding the people to write the law on parchment scrolls
By instructing Moses alone to communicate God's commands
questions.correctAnswer: By assigning tribes to publicly pronounce blessings and curses and having Levites declare the covenant, it involves all Israel in covenant renewal
questions.explanation: Verses 11-14 describe a public, communal ceremony where various tribes have roles in blessing or cursing, and the Levites loudly declare the covenant, showing collective responsibility for obedience.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 27:25 say about taking a reward to slay an innocent person, and what virtue does this condemn?
options: It curses taking a bribe to kill the innocent, condemning corruption and injustice
It blesses those who defend the innocent
It requires offering peace offerings for justice
It commands the building of an altar for atonement
questions.correctAnswer: It curses taking a bribe to kill the innocent, condemning corruption and injustice
questions.explanation: Verse 25 pronounces a curse on anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person, teaching the virtue of justice and condemning corruption.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 27:24 curses a person who secretly strikes his neighbor, emphasizing accountability for hidden sins.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 24 curses those who secretly strike their neighbor, highlighting that even hidden wrongdoing is subject to God's judgment and underscoring the virtue of accountability.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 27.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 27, who were assigned to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people?
options: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, Benjamin
Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, Naphtali
Moses and the priests
All the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, Benjamin
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:12 states that Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin were set to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people.

questions.question: What specific instruction is given about the stones used to build the altar on Mount Ebal?
options: They must be whole stones, with no iron tool used on them
They should be carved with iron tools
They should be painted with red dye
They must be stacked without mortar
questions.correctAnswer: They must be whole stones, with no iron tool used on them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:5-6 commands that the altar be built of whole stones and that no iron tool shall be lifted upon them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the curses pronounced by the Levites in Deuteronomy 27?
options: Cursed be he who lieth with his sister
Cursed be he who steals from a neighbor
Cursed be he who perverts the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow
Cursed be he who takes reward to slay an innocent person
questions.correctAnswer: Cursed be he who steals from a neighbor
questions.explanation: While many social sins are cursed, theft itself is not explicitly cursed in this chapter; Deuteronomy 27:17 curses removing a neighbor's landmark, not stealing.

questions.question: What is the significance of the people responding 'Amen' after each curse pronounced by the Levites?
options: It signifies their agreement and acceptance of the law and curses
It is a call for silence
It is a ritual chant with no meaning
It indicates their rejection of the curse
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies their agreement and acceptance of the law and curses
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:15-26 repeatedly shows the people responding 'Amen,' which is an affirmation of agreement to the curses and the covenant requirements.

questions.question: Which group was charged to speak the curses aloud to all Israel?
options: The Levites
The priests
The elders
The prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:14 states that the Levites shall speak the curses with a loud voice to all Israel.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 27:19, who are specifically mentioned as recipients of just judgment that must not be perverted?
options: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
The priests, the Levites, and the elders
The king, the judges, and the prophets
The rich, the poor, and the foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly mentions the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow as those whose judgment must not be perverted.

questions.question: Which of these sexual sins is NOT explicitly cursed in Deuteronomy 27?
options: Lying with a father's wife
Lying with a sister
Lying with a mother-in-law
Lying with a cousin
questions.correctAnswer: Lying with a cousin
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:20-23 curses various forbidden sexual relations but does not mention lying with a cousin.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'curse' in Deuteronomy 27:15-26 most closely imply in the original context?
options: A solemn pronouncement of judgment or doom
A casual complaint
A blessing in disguise
An expression of anger
questions.correctAnswer: A solemn pronouncement of judgment or doom
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ארור' (arur) means a formal and solemn curse or denunciation, indicating divine judgment as seen in Deuteronomy 27:15-26.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 27:26 emphasize the importance of obedience to the law?
options: It curses anyone who does not confirm and obey all the words of the law
It promises wealth to those who obey
It allows partial obedience
It mainly focuses on temple sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It curses anyone who does not confirm and obey all the words of the law
questions.explanation: Verse 26 pronounces a curse on anyone who does not confirm all the words of the law to obey them, stressing full obedience.

questions.question: Which earlier biblical event is reflected in the setting of Deuteronomy 27 with stones being set up and the law being written on them?
options: The giving of the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea
The fall of Jericho's walls
The building of Solomon’s temple
questions.correctAnswer: The giving of the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: The setting of stones with the law written on them in Deuteronomy 27 echoes the covenant renewal and law-giving at Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:4-8).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of curses for disobedience found in Deuteronomy 27?
options: Galatians 3:10
Matthew 5:44
Romans 8:1
John 3:16
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 3:10
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:10 references the curse of not abiding by the law, echoing Deuteronomy 27’s theme of curses for disobedience.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 27:15-26 where a series of curses is pronounced and the people respond 'Amen'?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Allegory
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The repeated structure of 'Cursed be he that...' followed by 'And all the people shall say, Amen' is an example of parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which tribe is mentioned as standing on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses according to Deuteronomy 27?
options: Reuben
Simeon
Judah
Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:13 lists Reuben among the tribes standing on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 27 commands the people to write the words of the law on stones after crossing the Jordan River.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:2-3 instructs the people to set up stones and write all the words of the law on them after crossing the Jordan.

questions.question: True or False: The altar to be built on Mount Ebal was to be made with iron tools to ensure durability.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:5 specifically forbids lifting any iron tool upon the stones used for the altar.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the significance of setting up great stones and plastering them according to Deuteronomy 27?
options: To serve as a memorial and a reminder of the law
To build a defensive wall against enemies
To create a monument for the elders of Israel
To mark the graves of the patriarchs
questions.correctAnswer: To serve as a memorial and a reminder of the law
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:2-3 commands the people to set up great stones and plaster them, writing all the words of the law on them to remind Israel of God's commandments as they enter the promised land.

questions.question: What does the command to build the altar without using iron tools (Deuteronomy 27:5) reveal about God's nature?
options: God's holiness and requirement for purity in worship
God's preference for natural materials over metal
God's interest in technological simplicity
God's dislike of iron as a metal
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and requirement for purity in worship
questions.explanation: The prohibition of iron tools on the altar (Deuteronomy 27:5) emphasizes God's holiness and the need for sanctity in worship, reflecting His demand for pure and undefiled offerings.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 27:7, what is the purpose of offering peace offerings and eating there?
options: To rejoice before the LORD thy God
To appease the gods of the land
To demonstrate military victory
To fulfill a social custom
questions.correctAnswer: To rejoice before the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly states that the peace offerings are for rejoicing before the LORD, indicating worship and celebration in God's presence.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by Moses' declaration in Deuteronomy 27:9 about Israel becoming the people of the LORD?
options: The doctrine of election and covenant relationship
The doctrine of universal salvation
The doctrine of reincarnation
The doctrine of self-righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of election and covenant relationship
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 27:9 states Israel has become the people of the LORD, teaching the doctrine of God's sovereign election and covenant relationship with His chosen people.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is reflected in the command to obey all His statutes and commandments in Deuteronomy 27:10?
options: God's sovereignty and righteous authority
God's mercy and forgiveness
God's omnipresence
God's omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty and righteous authority
questions.explanation: By commanding obedience to His statutes (Deuteronomy 27:10), God demonstrates His sovereign right to rule and His righteous authority over His people.

questions.question: What does the division of tribes to bless on Mount Gerizim and to curse on Mount Ebal (Deuteronomy 27:12-13) symbolize in the redemptive narrative?
options: The covenant blessings and curses contingent on obedience
The division of Israel into northern and southern kingdoms
The allocation of tribal territories
The separation of priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant blessings and curses contingent on obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 symbolize the covenantal principle that obedience to God results in blessings, while disobedience brings curses, reflecting God's justice throughout redemptive history.

questions.question: How does the pronouncement of curses on specific sins in Deuteronomy 27:15-26 relate to the doctrine of sin and its consequences?
options: Sin leads to separation from God and divine judgment
Sin is insignificant and easily overlooked
Sin is a social construct without spiritual impact
Sin only affects human relationships, not God
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to separation from God and divine judgment
questions.explanation: The series of curses in verses 15-26 illustrate that sin incurs God's judgment, emphasizing separation from His covenant blessings and holiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Old Testament laws are merely cultural and lack divine authority. What does Deuteronomy 27:1-10 actually teach about the nature of God's law?
options: God’s law is eternal, authoritative, and requires obedience
God’s law is optional and symbolic
God’s law is outdated and replaced
God’s law is only for priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: God’s law is eternal, authoritative, and requires obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 1-10 affirm the law’s divine origin, permanent authority, and call for obedience, countering sceptical claims about its dispensability.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Deuteronomy 27:5-6 and Deuteronomy 27:26 convey about worship and obedience?
options: True worship requires pure offerings and complete obedience to God's law
Worship is independent of obedience
Obedience is irrelevant if offerings are made
Worship should be secret and hidden
questions.correctAnswer: True worship requires pure offerings and complete obedience to God's law
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize pure, uncut stones for the altar (pure worship), while 27:26 curses those who do not obey all the law, together teaching that worship and obedience are inseparable.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed by the Levites loudly proclaiming the curses in Deuteronomy 27:14-26?
options: God’s justice in condemning sin
God’s hiddenness
God’s passivity
God’s indifference
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in condemning sin
questions.explanation: The Levites' loud proclamation of curses (27:14-26) reveals God’s justice in clearly condemning various sins to maintain holiness among His people.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 27:3-4 reflect God's faithfulness in the broader biblical narrative?
options: God fulfills His promise to give a land flowing with milk and honey
God changes His promises based on Israel's performance
God abandons His people in exile
God requires human effort to earn the land
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His promise to give a land flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 recall God’s promise to the patriarchs, showing His faithfulness in bringing Israel into the promised land as part of redemptive history.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the command in Deuteronomy 27:8 to write the law very plainly on the stones?
options: God desires clear and accessible revelation for His people
God prefers secret and mysterious laws
God’s law is only for the learned priests
God’s law is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God desires clear and accessible revelation for His people
questions.explanation: Verse 8’s instruction to write the law clearly shows God’s intent for His people to understand and obey His commands, underscoring the accessibility of divine revelation.

questions.question: What narrative arc does the setting of the altar on Mount Ebal in Deuteronomy 27:4-7 contribute to in the story of Israel?
options: The establishment of covenant worship in the promised land
The destruction of pagan altars
The division of the kingdom
The exile to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of covenant worship in the promised land
questions.explanation: Mount Ebal altar (verses 4-7) marks Israel’s formal covenant renewal and worship upon entering the promised land, a pivotal moment in the redemptive narrative.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Deuteronomy 27:15 and Deuteronomy 27:17 provide about idolatry and social justice?
options: Both idolatry and injustice are abominations that incur God's curse
Idolatry is acceptable if social justice is practiced
Social justice is unrelated to idolatry
Only idolatry is condemned, not injustice
questions.correctAnswer: Both idolatry and injustice are abominations that incur God's curse
questions.explanation: Verse 15 condemns graven images and verse 17 condemns moving landmarks (injustice), jointly teaching that both false worship and social injustice provoke divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 27:25 illustrate the biblical principle regarding the integrity of justice?
options: Taking bribes to kill an innocent person is cursed by God
Justice can be compromised for political gain
Innocent life has no special protection
Justice is a human invention without divine mandate
questions.correctAnswer: Taking bribes to kill an innocent person is cursed by God
questions.explanation: Verse 25 condemns accepting a bribe to slay an innocent person, affirming God's demand for justice and protection of innocent life.
